title: Resolution in Propositional Logic
subtopics: CNF representation as sets of sets
Resolution rule: from {L, …} and {¬L, …} derive their union minus L
Empty clause □ as witness of unsatisfiability
Soundness and completeness of ground resolution
Connection to DPLL and SAT solvers

definitions.definition: From clauses C₁ = {L} ∪ R₁ and C₂ = {¬L} ∪ R₂, derive the resolvent R₁ ∪ R₂.
A resolution proof that derives the empty clause □, proving unsatisfiability.
Resolution applied to ground (variable-free) clauses in propositional logic.

algorithms: Resolution refutation: repeatedly apply resolution rule until □ or saturation
formulas: Res(C₁, C₂) = (C₁ \ {L}) ∪ (C₂ \ {¬L}) where L ∈ C₁ and ¬L ∈ C₂
examples: Showing p → q, p ⊨ q by converting to CNF and applying resolution
exercises: Prove the associativity, commutativity, idempotency of ∨ and ∧.
Apply resolution to a given CNF formula to check satisfiability.
learning_objectives: Understand the resolution proof system and its motivation.
Represent clauses and CNF as sets.
Construct a resolution refutation to prove unsatisfiability.
